**Continuous 2.34.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.34.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.34.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.34.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.34.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.34.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.34.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.34.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.34.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.34.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.34.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.34.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.32.0

This release fixes the prompt cache misses on a local server once a long conversation fills the window. The point where the oldest messages are cut no longer moves by a message every few requests, so a 330k-token conversation is no longer read again from the start; a long agent loop compacts at a tool round instead of dropping the oldest turns; and Compact now is offered before the drop, including after a request that already dropped them. Web search gets its own `web.search` settings with SearXNG or your own endpoint, a web fetch that fails now says why and whether retrying helps, and a secret read followed by a network call always asks (and is the one call IDGAF refuses).

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### New

- Web search reads `web.search` in your own `config.yaml`: `provider: searxng` (your SearXNG server, also chosen by a `url` with no provider) or `provider: custom` (your own endpoint, `GET` in the SearXNG shape or `POST` with a `{"q": "..."}` body, the shape of Claude Desktop's custom search server). `maxResults` and `safeSearch` are in force. Search stays off until you pick a provider, and `@web` says why when it is not available.
- A workspace, assistant or hub config may only tighten search: `provider: off`, lower limits or a stricter `safeSearch`. A provider, URL or key it names is ignored with a notice.
- Search requests send `User-Agent: Continuous-User/<major>.<minor>`, with no info URL, or your `web.userAgent` preset.

### Behaviour changes

- Your message now also waits with Compact now and Continue anyway when the last request already dropped the oldest messages to fit, even if the context meter shows the conversation under the limit (the app and the server count tokens a little differently). The notice says the conversation is already past the point where the oldest turns are dropped. Nothing waits when there is nothing to compact (below 70% of the window, or with `contextManagement.plannedCompaction: false`), or after Continue anyway for the same plan.
- A long agent loop on a local server now compacts when the conversation reaches the context limit, instead of dropping the oldest messages between two tool rounds. A summary already prepared is used at once; otherwise one is made from the conversation the server still holds ("Generating conversation summary" shows while it runs, and Stop stops it). Loop items and resumed turns do the same. Nothing asks, and the oldest-messages drop is still the fallback when planned compaction is off (`contextManagement.plannedCompaction: false`), after Continue anyway at the compaction hold, or when the summary fails. On cloud providers only a summary that is already prepared is used.
- Planned compaction can now cut inside one long turn, at a tool round, so a loop that started from a single message can be compacted.
- The compaction hold now comes before the oldest messages are dropped on a local server: it compared the prompt with 85% of the window, while the drop starts at 85% of the window less the 5% headroom of the token calibration.
- **A secret, then a network call, asks at every level and is refused at IDGAF.** Once a session has read a secret's content (a protected secret file such as `.env`, `~/.npmrc` or `~/.aws/credentials` read with a file tool, with a command such as `cat`, `Get-Content`, `grep` or `base64`, from a redirect, or sent by `curl -d @.env` and the like; or a command that prints a credential), a call that can send data out (a fetch, `curl`, `ssh`, `gh api`, a push, a package publish, a tool of an MCP server you have not marked `trusted` in your own `permissions.yaml`) asks you at Manual, Cautious, Automatic and Permissive, even where a level, an allow rule or `--allow` would have run it, and Automatic's reviewer never answers it. Headless, where nobody can be asked, it is refused. At IDGAF it is refused, with or without Questions at IDGAF, and never asked: it is the one call IDGAF refuses. The refusal starts `Refused at IDGAF:` and names what read the secret and where the call would send it. Only naming the file (`echo .env`, `ls .env`, `test -f .env`, `git status`) marks nothing. This holds whether or not `taintedSessionRule` is on, and `/untaint` does not clear it; a new session starts without it. Marking the session writes one `secret-read` record to the audit trail, with the path cut to the file's name.
- **Automatic refuses a write to a PowerShell profile.** `Documents\WindowsPowerShell\*profile.ps1` and `Documents\PowerShell\*profile.ps1`, under your home folder or a OneDrive-redirected Documents, and `$PROFILE`, now count as files that change what runs later: they ask at Manual, Cautious and Permissive, are refused at Automatic, and run at IDGAF with the decision recording that Automatic would have refused them. With `protect-config` off they are not refused.
- **The sandbox read policy hides credential stores and policy folders.** With the sandbox on, commands cannot read the OS credential stores (`~/Library/Keychains` on macOS; `~/.local/share/keyrings`, `~/.local/share/kwalletd` and `~/.password-store` on Linux and WSL2) or a project's `.continuous` and `.continue` folders (their `plans/` folders stay readable), besides `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config/gh` and the home policy folders as before. `~/.npmrc` is now readable in the sandbox (still write-protected), and `~/.gitconfig` stays readable; reading `~/.npmrc` with a tool or a command such as `cat` still counts as reading a secret.
- A web fetch that does not return a page (`fetch_url_content` in the editor, `Fetch` in `cn`) now comes back as a normal tool result that says what happened and whether retrying can help, instead of a bare error such as `HTTP 404 Not Found`. Each result has a typed code: `not-found`, `gone`, `forbidden`, `auth-required`, `rate-limited` (with the wait from `Retry-After`), `server-error`, `client-error`, `timeout`, `dns`, `dns-temporary`, `tls`, `connection`, `not-text`, `needs-js` (an application shell that needs JavaScript), `needs-cookies` (a redirect loop that sets cookies, such as a sign-in or consent wall) and `refused`. In the editor the code is the result's `status`. Response bodies are never quoted.
- The existing refusals (a non-http URL, a user name or password in the URL, a credential-shaped value, a redirect to a non-public address) keep their wording and now end with "Do not retry it unchanged."
- `@url` shows the first sentence of the same outcome when a page cannot be read, for example `Not found: docs.example.com answered 404 for /v2/guide.`
- `CONTINUOUS_WEB_SEARCH_URL` and `CONTINUOUS_WEB_SEARCH_KEY` still work, now with a deprecation notice: use `web.search.url` and `web.search.apiKey`. They are not used when `web.search` names a provider or a URL.
- A key typed into `web.search.apiKey` (rather than `${{ secrets.NAME }}`) is used with a warning in the config errors and in `continuous doctor config`. A later minor release refuses it.

### Fixes

- On a local server, once a conversation no longer fit the window, the point where the oldest messages were cut moved by one message every few requests, so the whole conversation was read again (about 70 s at 330k tokens) with "Likely cause: message 2 changed: an answer; the oldest messages were dropped to fit". The token calibration moved the budget on every request; it now changes the budget only when the measured ratio moves more than 2.5%.
- The prompt cache miss notice now says when a miss came from dropping the oldest messages, and when that happened between an agent's tool rounds, and offers Compact now.
- `cn`'s `Fetch` no longer leaves console errors silenced after a failed fetch.

### Upgrade notes

- **Local servers.** After updating, a conversation past the context limit compacts instead of dropping its oldest turns, when planned compaction is on (the default). Set `contextManagement.plannedCompaction: false` to keep the old drop.
- **Web search** is off until you set `web.search` in your own `config.yaml`. `CONTINUOUS_WEB_SEARCH_URL` and `CONTINUOUS_WEB_SEARCH_KEY` still work, with a deprecation notice.
- **IDGAF** now refuses a network call after a secret was read in the same session; start a new session to clear it.
- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** No new host.
